builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Asymmetric Speculative Decoding: Unlocking In-Context Learning in Draft Models
summary: Replaces symmetric-prompt speculative decoding by giving the draft model task-relevant example solutions while the target model keeps the original prompt, converting the draft's job from reasoning to simulating the target. Costs extra prompt tokens and context for the draft on every speculation round, plus implementation effort since standard serving frameworks assume identical prompts for draft and target. Can fail when example solutions do not match the query distribution, when added draft context erodes the latency budget, or on tasks where the acceptance-rate gain does not offset verification overhead.
rationale: It is training-free and increases draft acceptance by prompting the small draft model with example solutions instead of the raw task, but the gain depends on workload-specific prompt design and acceptance behavior that must be validated on the reader's serving stack.
technique: Asymmetric prompts for speculative decoding draft models

claims.statement: Replaces symmetric-prompt speculative decoding by giving the draft model task-relevant example solutions while the target model keeps the original prompt, converting the draft's job from reasoning to simulating the target. Costs extra prompt tokens and context for the draft on every speculation round, plus implementation effort since standard serving frameworks assume identical prompts for draft and target. Can fail when example solutions do not match the query distribution, when added draft context erodes the latency budget, or on tasks where the acceptance-rate gain does not offset verification overhead.
Reports 2.29x to 4.95x speedup over autoregressive decoding on reasoning, code generation, and summarization, outperforming standard speculative decoding without retraining.
